label: H.R. 9538

latest_action.text: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.

selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: H.R. 9538 amends title XVIII of the Social Security Act to establish Medicare Part A coverage for certain residential substance use disorder services. It defines three distinct levels of residential care (clinically managed low-intensity, clinically managed high-intensity, and medically managed), sets standards for facilities and programs offering these services, includes these facilities as Medicare providers, and directs the creation of a prospective per diem payment system.

affected_groups.effect: Gain Part A coverage for residential substance use disorder services, including bed and board, clinical services, and medical monitoring.
Can enroll as Medicare providers, must meet specified accreditation and staffing standards, and will receive payments under a new prospective payment system.
affected_groups.group: Residential substance use disorder facilities and programs

key_provisions: Establishes Medicare Part A coverage for clinically managed low-intensity, clinically managed high-intensity, and medically managed residential substance use disorder services.
Requires periodic review and reaffirmation of a patient's need for care, at least every 30 days for clinically managed services and at least every 10 days for medically managed services.
Defines standards for clinically managed low-intensity, clinically managed high-intensity, and medically managed programs, including staffing, assessments, and clinical services.
Adds clinically managed and medically managed residential substance use disorder facilities as approved Medicare providers.
Directs the Secretary to develop a per diem prospective payment system for residential substance use disorder services starting on or after October 1, 2026.
